comparator.name: Medicine (Geneeskunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 Medicine EER applies to the first entering cohort of the new De Nieuwe Utrechtse Arts curriculum and establishes a 180-EC bachelor comprising a 165-EC compulsory Medicine major and 15 EC of genuine profile space. Appendix 1b gives the complete DNUA major. The four 3-EC carousel courses are all compulsory: three are taken in Year 1 and one in Year 2, with order depending on group allocation. The EER is used for exact credits where the current student overview remains provisional: Bewegen & Waarnemen and Levensloop are each 10 EC in the adopted EER, not the earlier 9.5-EC webpage figures. The 15-EC profile space is preserved generically rather than filled with invented electives. All 180 EC are thereby accounted for.

routeSelection.basis: DNUA is the formally adopted curriculum for all students entering Medicine in 2026–27; the predecessor CRU+ curriculum accepted its final entrants in 2025–26. DNUA is therefore the only cohort-applicable curriculum for this Fall-2026 comparison and is selected independently of UCR fit.

exception.reason: Utrecht's Medicine bachelor integrates organ-system biomedical science with compulsory clinical reasoning, practical clinical skills, workplace learning, patient and community experience, professional behaviour, complex-care challenges, pharmacotherapy, longitudinal interdisciplinary formation and a medical research thesis. UCR can build a strong biomedical and health-sciences programme, but it does not offer patient interviewing and physical examination, clinical skills assessment, supervised workplace learning in health-care settings, integrated diagnostic reasoning, longitudinal medical-professional formation or organ-system clinical teaching across circulation, respiration, neurology, psychiatry, digestion, urogenital and hormonal medicine, movement, lifespan care, haematology and oncology. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be biomedical science with psychology and public health, not a defensible Medicine curriculum.
exception.curriculumContext: The adopted 2026–27 DNUA curriculum accounts for all 180 EC through a compulsory 165-EC Medicine major and 15 EC of approved profile space. The major combines integrated biomedical and organ-system courses, four compulsory health/innovation/community carousels, three years of Discipline Overstijgend Onderwijs and Praktisch Lijnonderwijs, two years of Clinical Reasoning, Year-3 workplace learning, complex clinical care, Health Humanities, Haematology & Oncology, Pharmacology & Pharmacotherapy, the interuniversity medical progress test, and a 13-EC Science & Bachelor Thesis component.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide substantial life-science foundations. HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease provide advanced biomedical content; HCBGATE102 Introduction to Brain & Behavior, HCBCOGN112 Neurobiology and Psychology courses cover brain, behaviour and mental-health perspectives; HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health and ethics, sociology and communication courses add population, societal and ethical perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no clinical-skills or physical-examination course, no patient-interviewing sequence, no supervised clinical or workplace-learning component, no integrated diagnostic-reasoning progression, no longitudinal medical professional-behaviour curriculum, and no comprehensive clinical organ-system sequence. These compulsory programme-wide medical gaps cannot be repaired by selecting adjacent biomedical, psychology or public-health courses.
